citation: Ostrowska L, Smarkusz-Zarzecka J, Muszyńska A, et al. High-Fat or High-Carbohydrate Meal—Does It Affect the Metabolism of Men with Excess Body Weight?. Nutrients. 2022;14(14):2876.
protocol: Two isocaloric 450 kcal liquid meals on separate days: high-fat Calogen (Nutricia; 95 mL; 96% energy fat, 4% carbohydrate, 0% protein) and high-carbohydrate Nutridrink Fat Free (300 mL; 89% carbohydrate, 11% protein, 0% fat). Venous blood at 0, 30, 60, 120, 180, 240 min.
population: 26 men aged 19-60 without carbohydrate disorders: 13 normal body weight (control group GC) and 13 overweight/obese (GS); Poland (Bialystok).

reports.where: Table 3: concentration at each time point and AUC, per group and per meal

note: A near-pure fat load and a near-pure carbohydrate drink in the same men, with the full time course in one table; use the normal-weight group. The insulin unit is printed as 'IU/mL' (read it as µIU/mL); the statistics section says values are mean and SD. Meal kinds: fat load, liquid meal.
